{
  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both final plans support the same consequential outcome: retain the installed adapter, contain its partial commits in a private snapshot, publish once through parent-owned atomic replacement, preserve unrelated inventory, and recover through idempotent retry. Both distinguish precommit failure from committed publication with lost acknowledgment and leave real CLI, interruption and recovery acceptance due implementation. A supports a broader observed WAL-normalization path; B explicitly rejects unsupported journal states. The supplied request does not establish that this difference changes the required outcome. B's additional worker observations and A's more detailed decomposition do not demonstrate superior final quality.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Installed adapter applies rows in private short-lived worker; parent alone publishes.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.summary",
      "consequence": "Adapter commits cannot expose a partial batch through the live inventory; publication authority remains separate."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "SQLite backup snapshots all existing tables, then installed adapter updates inventory only on that snapshot, preserving unrelated state.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Structure",
      "consequence": "B reaches the same isolation and preservation design while retaining the installed adapter."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Before replace failures keep B; after replace N is committed even if acknowledgment/directory fsync fails.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items[1].context",
      "consequence": "Recovery has a coherent commit boundary and does not promise rollback after completed publication."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "termination after commit yields complete new inventory with acknowledgement uncertainty and safe repeat.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, AD-6",
      "consequence": "B preserves the same necessary distinction between interruption before publication and response loss afterward."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "After explicit closes normalization returned delete, -wal/-journal were absent but -shm remained.",
      "locator": "A.planning_artifacts: run/notes/planning-experiments.md, P1 final outcome and decision consequences",
      "consequence": "A's selected journal policy follows an observed local boundary; its earlier failed all-sidecars-absent checks are not represented as passes."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "WAL/sidecars are fail-closed preflight conditions, not support claims.",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.summary",
      "consequence": "B makes its narrower publication boundary explicit. Implementing and verifying those guards remains required."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Actual CLI/kill-at-publication/recovery command tests remain W3 due, not waived by API passes.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items[1].context",
      "consequence": "Runtime characterization and future component results cannot substitute for requested product acceptance."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "All worker protocol, termination and prepublication sequencing tests are component/CLI cases due implementation;",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.work_items[1].context",
      "consequence": "B likewise keeps worker feasibility observations separate from acceptance of the actual importer."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "A's initial plan already contained the supported publication policy, worker isolation and W1→W2→W3 acceptance ownership. Its review made meaningful handoff repairs: TC_8 still requested a journal-policy decision already made, and the authoritative command list omitted W2's component suite. It also corrected experiment accounting. The core architecture and dependency order remained unchanged. B's initial plan correctly kept publication feasibility conditional and gated progression on resolving it. Review supplied scoped publication evidence, clarified fixture interfaces and journal guards, then repaired the inaccessible adapter-handle closure requirement by selecting a waited worker process. B's earlier strategy review also added staged-prefix interruption coverage. B required more substantive review rework, but its initial conditionality was not false readiness, and the repaired final plan reaches the same consequential outcome.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "Both could legitimately reject direct-live application and caller rollback from inspected adapter source; the earlier partial-write observations corroborated that conclusion. A reused earlier baseline, staging and runtime evidence, then used its publication attempts to resolve WAL and residual-sidecar behavior. B reused adapter characterization, strengthened E1 with independent private-stage readback, and used E2 to observe worker success, partial failure, interruption and retry. These observations support different parts of the decisions without becoming product passes. A's source-grounded worker choice need not have an additional prototype to be legitimate. Unchanged baseline evidence remains reusable after documentation-only edits.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [
    "No demonstrated seed mutation, unauthorized external action, material resource leak or loss of required implementation acceptance appears in the retained record.",
    "B's refusal of WAL, sidecars and other unsupported targets limits compatibility; A instead plans observed local normalization. No required WAL-success case is established, so this is not a demonstrated lost requirement.",
    "A's known-missing-module invocations and additional experiment launches are cost observations, not demonstrated correctness regressions. Its final record explicitly accounts for four disposable script launches overall.",
    "Retained scripts, outputs or disposable scratch data do not establish material harm without an effect on sensitive data, authority, running resources, experiment validity or the inventory outcome."
  ],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "A's empty decision_rework list underreports meaningful review repair: the retained review identifies contradictory journal-policy instructions and a missing authoritative component-suite command. Its narrower statement that the core design and dependency order did not change remains accurate.",
    "Neither individual judgment's final correctness or readiness conclusion is contradicted by the supplied plans. In particular, B's revised A5 characterizes runtime signaling while explicitly retaining W1 helper implementation and validation; it does not claim that helper already exists.",
    "B's claim that repeated guide reads at events 40 and 96 added no useful information cannot be independently resolved from this paired view. The omitted command transcript is needed to verify the repetition and context; this remains an unresolved cost claim."
  ],
  "confidence": "high",
  "limits": [
    "This compares planning outcomes only. Neither importer nor its retained feature acceptance tests were implemented; the passing product suite contains one existing baseline test.",
    "Some cited probe outputs and source inspections are represented through retained notes and judgments rather than reproduced raw execution records. Exact command-level claims cannot all be independently audited here.",
    "Observed mechanisms apply to the characterized local runtime and filesystem. Product guard behavior, worker integration and actual CLI recovery remain due; power-loss and arbitrary-filesystem guarantees are unestablished.",
    "No required external boundary is unavailable. Out-of-scope external services and unimplemented local acceptance should not be conflated with blocked access."
  ]
}
